name: dstack-trixie-arm64-minimal
description: Minimal dstack-derived ARM64 base VM image: Debian trixie rootfs from the upstream dstack snapshot pin, dstack squashfs+dm-verity root protocol, dstack checksum-manifest identity, source-built dstack-lineage kernel; TDX/GPU/KMS/gateway content excluded.

workload_interface.transport: raw disk vdc: uncompressed tar at offset 0 with SHA256SUMS
workload_interface.executor: trusted guest supervisor (measured image content) drives dockerd on a root-only socket and runs docker compose up --abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from runner
workload_interface.provenance: same external-workload contract as base-vm-foundation/arm64-compatibility lanes

identity.os_image_hash_definition: sha256(sha256sum.txt) where sha256sum.txt covers Image, initramfs.cpio.gz, metadata.json, rootfs.squashfs.verity
identity.upstream_os_image_hash_definition: sha256(sha256sum.txt) over ovmf.fd bzImage initramfs.cpio.gz metadata.json measurement.tdx.cbor (rootfs bound via metadata.cmdline verity hash + TEE measurements)
identity.delta_note: no firmware / TEE measurement artifacts exist on ARM64/Mac; the rootfs image bytes are checksummed directly so verified-byte loading binds them without a TEE

verity_parameters.format: squashfs (zstd) + appended dm-verity hash tree, mksquashfs -tar from a sorted deterministic tar stream

deltas_vs_upstream: architecture arm64 (upstream x86-64/TDX); kernel built from the SAME pinned linux-6.18.40.tar.xz via arm64 defconfig + arch-neutral subset of upstream kernel.config (upstream: x86_64_defconfig + full TDX/SEV config and 10 TDX patches, dropped as x86-TEE-specific)

no OVMF/SEV firmware, no UKI, no measurement.{tdx,gcp,aws}.cbor: platform has no TEE measurement path; identity is the checksum manifest + verity root hash + cmdline, all bound in metadata.json and enforced by verified-byte loading
rootfsverity included in sha256sum.txt (upstream excludes the rootfs image; it is bound transitively via cmdline+MRTD)

guest init execs the trusted supervisor /usr/bin/dsmack-supervisor instead of systemd /sbin/init: appliance VM with external workload policy; systemd present in the rootfs only as dependency content, never executed (boot-time and minimality delta; documented, reviewable)

packages: upstream mkosi.conf Packages minus tpm2-tools, wireguard-tools, chrony, nvattest xmlsec libs, debug/net utilities (netcat, traceroute, pciutils, usbutils, fdisk, dosfstools, gdisk, parted, xfsprogs, rsync, pigz, fuse3, acpid, numactl, systemd-boot*), keeping the container stack + verity + CA bundle + busybox
no dstack guest agent / gateway / kms / key-provider services in the image (separate milestones per reconciliation; not silently completed)
kernel container-stack features built-in (=y) instead of modules (=m) so no module loading is needed before the container stack starts

debootstrap --foreign stage-1 rootfs (unpack without maintainer scripts) instead of mkosi chroot install: host has no binfmt/qemu for arm64 and global binfmt registration is out of scope; consequence: dpkg states stay 'Unpacked', packages are never configured — acceptable because no dpkg/systemd runs in the guest; all functionality used is unpacked file content. Upstream mkosi runs full install in its x86 chroot.

cmdline: console=hvc0 (Mac HVF + harness contract) instead of ttyS0; x86-only tokens mce=off/pci=noearly/tsc=reliable/no-kvmclock dropped; random.trust_cpu/random.trust_bootloader dropped because the RANDOM_TRUST_* Kconfig symbols were removed from the kernel before 6.18 (upstream's x86 line still carries random.trust_cpu=y — inert there; observed here, not copied); dstack.rootfs_device= added for the unpartitioned raw image

kernel 6.18 removed the legacy ip_tables family (IP_NF_IPTABLES/IP_NF_FILTER/IP_NF_NAT/IP_NF_TARGET_MASQUERADE): filtering/NAT assert the nftables-era path (NETFILTER_XTABLES/NF_CONNTRACK/NF_NAT/NF_TABLES + NETFILTER_XT_TARGET_MASQUERADE =y); the vendored upstream config checker caught each clamp during bring-up (4 rejected fragments before this final one)
excluded_by_policy: runsc/gVisor (separate runsc-qualification lane owns that mode)
